label: Presenter notes — not on-screen source content

opening: We hear the word Jannah all the time.
We ask Allah for Jannah. We make du'a for Jannah. We talk about wanting to be among its people.
But before we talk about what it takes to get there, I want to begin somewhere else.
What has Allah actually told us about Jannah?
What is this place that we're spending our lives trying to reach?
So for this first part, I just want us to look at how Allah and the Prophet ﷺ describe it.
the-promise: Notice something about the way Allah describes Jannah here.
There is this idea of permanence.
Think about the beautiful things that we experience here.
A moment that we wish could last forever eventually passes.
But Allah describes the fruit of Jannah as lasting, and its shade as lasting.
There's no anxiety that the beautiful thing you're experiencing is about to disappear.
And Allah also begins this description by mentioning rivers.
And those rivers are described in even more detail elsewhere in the Qur'an.
the-rivers: Allah doesn't only tell us that there are rivers in Jannah.
He tells us what some of them are.
And notice again that Allah removes the defects we're familiar with here.
The water is unaltered. The taste of the milk doesn't change.
Things here deteriorate. They spoil. They change.
But the descriptions of Jannah repeatedly remove those limitations.
And then Allah mentions something alongside all of these physical blessings: forgiveness from their Lord.
So Jannah isn't simply about receiving beautiful things.
You're there because Allah has forgiven you.
beyond-imagination: This hadith is really important before we continue.
Because I'm saying words like river, tree, fruit and garden.
And every time I say one of those words, your mind automatically creates an image.
If I say river, you're probably imagining some version of a river you've seen.
If I say tree, you're imagining a tree.
But Allah tells us that He has prepared something no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that we haven't even imagined.
So these descriptions allow us to understand something about Jannah.
But we shouldn't make the mistake of thinking the picture in our heads is the reality.
Whatever we're imagining, the reality is greater.
the-gardens: Surah Ar-Rahman gives us one of the most detailed descriptions of Jannah in the Qur'an.
Allah takes us through garden after garden.
There are branches, flowing springs, fruits, shade and places of rest.
And then He describes another pair of gardens.
There are gushing springs, fruit, palm trees and pomegranates.
But there's something else happening throughout the passage.
'So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?'
We hear it again and again as the descriptions continue.
It's almost as though we're being taken from one blessing to another and repeatedly being reminded:
Who gave you all of this?
Every beautiful thing being described is a gift from Allah.
abundance-rest-peace: Surah Al-Waqi'ah gives us another picture.
Fruit that isn't cut off or forbidden.
But one of my favourite details here actually has nothing to do with food or scenery.
Allah says that they won't hear ill speech or sinful speech.
Think about how much of the exhaustion of this dunya comes from people.
So Jannah isn't only physical comfort.
the-first-to-enter: The Prophet ﷺ doesn't only describe the place.
He describes the people who enter it.
The first group will shine like the full moon.
Their sweat will smell like musk.
And they're described as resembling their father Adam, sixty cubits tall.
Even the ordinary unpleasant functions of our bodies here are gone.
And another narration gives us something I think is even more beautiful.
There won't be hatred or differences between the people of Jannah. Their hearts will be like one heart.
So Allah doesn't only transform the world around you.
The things inside us that cause pain, resentment and conflict don't follow us into Jannah.
the-tree: And then we get a description that almost breaks our sense of scale.
The Prophet ﷺ tells us that there is a tree in Jannah whose shade is so vast that a rider could travel underneath it for a hundred years and still not cross it.
For the shade of one tree.
And then remember the hadith we read earlier.
Whatever tree you're imagining right now is still being created by your mind using things you've already seen.
The reality of what Allah has prepared is beyond that.
the-greatest-reward: After everything we've just described, there is still something greater.
The Prophet ﷺ tells us that after the people of Jannah enter Paradise, Allah will ask them if they want anything more.
They've been saved from the Fire.
What could possibly be left to ask for?
And the Prophet ﷺ tells us that nothing they have been given will be more beloved to them than seeing their Lord.
After everything we just spent this entire section describing...
That is the greatest reward of Jannah.
